column5: ICO B2B (read in full): live B2B calls must not go to numbers on the CTPS or TPS without consent, nor to anyone who has objected; the caller must say who is calling, display a number and give contact details or a Freephone number if asked; screen against both the CTPS and the TPS because sole traders and some partnerships register on the TPS; automated B2B calls need specific consent.

ICO B2B: if you cannot tell whether a contact is a corporate subscriber or an individual subscriber (sole trader or ordinary partnership), treat it as an individual and get consent or meet the soft opt-in before emailing; corporate opt-outs are not strictly required by PECR for email, but you should honour them, and a named contact has an absolute UK GDPR right to object to direct marketing that you must follow.

ICO B2B and prospecting sources: details from a company website, Companies House, social media or press articles are still subject to PECR for calls, emails and social direct messages, and to UK GDPR if they name a person; business cards put into a contacts database bring UK GDPR into play; people on professional networking sites are usually there in a personal professional capacity, so messaging them is not B2B marketing; tell contacts within one month if you collect their data from a third party or public source. Directly relevant to the course's ten lead sources.

ICO B2B lawful basis and records: consent or legitimate interests are the usual UK GDPR bases (legitimate interests needs the three-part test: purpose, necessity, balance); post is not covered by PECR; keep objections on a suppression list rather than deleting them. Fits the CRM record-keeping lesson.
